title: About five turns on one idea
statement: Keep a comprehension exchange on one idea for about five turns, each reply building on the learner's answer rather than only judging it, and measure turns per conversation.
example: One rulebook asks for at least 5 turns on one idea: open question, child, challenge, child, then a recast or extension to close.
detail: A grade-3 reading rulebook's law on the third turn says evaluation-only replies end the conversation and asks for at least five turns on one idea, and a reading quality canon applied in a grade-5 audit gives the shape: open question, child, challenge, child, then a recast or extension to close. The audit's notes trace the structure to a brief on opportunities to respond, which also sorts the second turn by the kind of answer, from a full and correct one to no response.
against: Its source covers only the earliest grades: "written for K–2; use as design principle for G5, not age authority." (`grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/g5-audit/KB-NOTES.md`, lines 140-141). The grade-3 rulebook also rules that full credit carries no further ask, "A passed answer never renders "Make it even stronger" / "One more thing" / "Try this"." (`grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/01-NON-NEGOTIABLES.md`, lines 32-33), which a challenge after a passed answer would break. The synthesis was "Written for PreK to Grade 2 and stated as out of scope for "grades 3 and above"" (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md`, line 12), and which measures to build is left open: "Choose which measures to operationalize in the app." (line 200).

evidence.quote: Evaluation-only replies end the conversation. Strive-for-Five: ≥5 turns on one idea.
The conversation follows the Strive-for-Five shape: open question → child → challenge → child → recast/extend close (~5 turns).
Structure: open question → child → scaffolded challenge → child → recast/extend close

A single question and answer is one exchange, not comprehension. Following *Strive-for-Five*, the app should treat about five turns as the shape of a comprehension conversation, which is also what the Speaking and Listening standards ask of young children (for example, “continue a conversation through multiple exchanges,” SL.K.1b and SL.1.1b).
Measure with three signals, not one: responses per minute, turns per conversation, and how much language the child produces, along with whether the app actually used the child’s answer.
Written for PreK to Grade 2 and stated as out of scope for "grades 3 and above"
Choose which measures to operationalize in the app.

citations.ref: Cabell & Zucker 2024, Using Strive-for-Five conversations to strengthen language comprehension in preschool through Grade One, The Reading Teacher
